subject: reported differentially methylated promoter regions does not contain differentially methylated bases

messages.author: 653d049a2e96ed7e
messages.subject: reported differentially methylated promoter regions does not contain differentially methylated bases
parts:
Hi,
I have (bismark aligned and sorted) 3 control SAMs and 3 treatement SAMs. First, I tried to find differentially methylated bases (attached script diffMeth.r) and later tried to find differentially methylated promoter region  (attached script promoterMeth.r).

In Diff-25p.txt you can see that there are differentially methylated based reported by methylKit. Here, I have included methylated bases only from X chromosome.

In Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt you can see X chromosome promoter region that are differentially methylated.
But, to my surprise differentially methylated bases (Diff-25p.txt) does not falls in any promoter region interval reported in Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt. For example, in Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt chrX:89409738 - 89409738 promoter region is diffrentially methylated, but there are not any differentially methylated bases within the region if you look at Diff-25p.txt.

Did I do something stupid ?


Regards,
Bishwa

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] reported differentially methylated promoter regions does not contain differentially methylated bases
parts:
I wouldn't expect the differentially methylated bases on promoters will be always overlapping with differentially methylated promoters from the regional analysis. One is looking at the bases, the other at regions and when you sum up the methylated and unmethylated bases overlapping with a region you change the statistics, it can go either way, it can push the region to be differentially methylated although individual bases are not DMCs in your thresholds. You see most of your differentially methylated promoters are borderline close to 25% threshold.

The proper way to check and report this it is to find all promoter overlapping DMCs and then check what percent of those promoters overlapping with DMCs are differentially methylated promoters from your promoterMeth.r script. If they never overlap there might be a problem.

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: b9c95d8a0ed19187
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] reported differentially methylated promoter regions does not contain differentially methylated bases
parts:
I figure it out !!!

this weighted.mean=FALSE will save me ! One of my 60 biological replicates with so much coverage on so much positions did drive the difference of methylation in a really strong way.

Thanks a lot for your help and for this tool, I will answer to the method discussion for further stuffs. I guess I will become a strong activist for the update of the tile test with weighted.mean=FALSE !

Le lundi 17 février 2014 11:48:20 UTC-5, Raphael Paul Emile a écrit :
Sorry for the disturbing format, you can assume I understand bed formats and tables in R.

I have some null q values, is that normal ?

We have so much samples that it s hard to send you the files for the tests, I just spot these interval with -48.75 % of methylation and I wanted to check in my initial data what does the single positions look like.
I guess it s not straight forward, my intervall is chr10 from 77155451 to 77155550:

bed :
chr10    77155451    77155550    *    0    0    -48.7489724216988

I can take all the interval positions over 5X in my bismarck output in the controls subjects :
http://nasty.mushroom.free.fr/trucs/control_myCpG.txt

The same for the cases :
http://nasty.mushroom.free.fr/trucs/case_myCpG.txt

Here you have everything ! Except that the filter by coverage is done with 99% and the normalzation is not done, but anyway I can t imagine how we get 48% of differences with those informations.

Thank you for your help !



Le vendredi 14 février 2014 19:22:49 UTC-5, Altuna Akalin a écrit :
In addition, if you used the same table you sent in bedtools it won't work, it has to be BED format to be used in bedtools.


On Sat, Feb 15, 2014 at 1:11 AM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:
the line number shouldn't be there but I guess it comes from the write.table  default argument. In any case, I can not replicate the error with the example data sets. you need to share more information.

I need subset of the data and your script that works with that subset that demonstrates the problem. If you can replicate the problem with one of the smaller chromosomes or part of a chromosome that would be good. 


On Fri, Feb 14, 2014 at 7:46 PM, Raphael Paul Emile <raphael...@gmail.com> wrote:
The line come from a txt that we did from the object table, what looks weird exactly ?
The head of the file :

"line" "chr" "start" "end" "strand" "pvalue" "qvalue" "meth.diff"
"1" "1" 10501 10600 "*" 0 0 5.68520504202106
"15" "1" 839351 839450 "*" 8.4821039081362e-14 3.83091276233629e-14 5.85733887513346

Sup question -> a null p value mean extreeeeeeme significance ?

We did what you said with bedtool intersect. All the positions in the bed resulting are present in the tile bed resulting for instance ...


Le vendredi 14 février 2014 13:05:33 UTC-5, Altuna Akalin a écrit :
check the region with findOverlaps() fromGRanges, you can coerce methylKit objects to GRanges, and verify if there is really no CpG overlapping. In addition, your object looks weird there might something wrong with the whole object or chromsome names. If you can find a bug or error, send subset of data and script that reproduces the problem.


On Fri, Feb 14, 2014 at 6:57 PM, <raphael...@gmail.com> wrote:
We have the same problem checking a region that have a meth.diff around -48% with a q value of 0, with 29 case and 29 controls.

"20833" "10" 77155451 77155550 "*" 0 0 -48.7489724216988

Now I am looking for positions in this interval and I cannot find any !

Le lundi 10 février 2014 18:49:12 UTC-5, Altuna Akalin a écrit :
I wouldn't expect the differentially methylated bases on promoters will be always overlapping with differentially methylated promoters from the regional analysis. One is looking at the bases, the other at regions and when you sum up the methylated and unmethylated bases overlapping with a region you change the statistics, it can go either way, it can push the region to be differentially methylated although individual bases are not DMCs in your thresholds. You see most of your differentially methylated promoters are borderline close to 25% threshold.

The proper way to check and report this it is to find all promoter overlapping DMCs and then check what percent of those promoters overlapping with DMCs are differentially methylated promoters from your promoterMeth.r script. If they never overlap there might be a problem.

Best,
Altuna


On Mon, Feb 10, 2014 at 2:59 PM, Bishwa Ghimire <bishwa....@btk.fi> wrote:
Hi,
I have (bismark aligned and sorted) 3 control SAMs and 3 treatement SAMs. First, I tried to find differentially methylated bases (attached script diffMeth.r) and later tried to find differentially methylated promoter region  (attached script promoterMeth.r).

In Diff-25p.txt you can see that there are differentially methylated based reported by methylKit. Here, I have included methylated bases only from X chromosome.

In Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt you can see X chromosome promoter region that are differentially methylated.
But, to my surprise differentially methylated bases (Diff-25p.txt) does not falls in any promoter region interval reported in Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt. For example, in Diff-25p-promoter-tss-features.txt chrX:89409738 - 89409738 promoter region is diffrentially methylated, but there are not any differentially methylated bases within the region if you look at Diff-25p.txt.

Did I do something stupid ?


Regards,
Bishwa
